slot.brief: Give an active voice sentence in simple past or present perfect tense; ask students to choose the correct passive form from four options.

stem: Select the option that correctly expresses the given sentence in the passive voice: The committee has rejected the new proposal.
options: The new proposal has been rejected by the committee.
The new proposal has rejected by the committee.
The new proposal was rejected by the committee.
The new proposal is being rejected by the committee.

verdicts.working: Present perfect passive uses “has been” + past participle: “The new proposal has been rejected by the committee.”
issues: The images labeled A–D show chemical structures and are unrelated to the grammar question.

working:
Active 'has rejected' (present perfect) becomes passive 'has been rejected' (has + been + past participle); the object 'the new proposal' becomes the subject and the doer is retained after 'by'. A omits 'been', C changes the tense to simple past, and D changes it to present continuous. Only B preserves both the tense and the meaning.

Independent check: Present perfect passive uses “has been” + past participle: “The new proposal has been rejected by the committee.”
solution: Present perfect passive is formed with $has/have + been +$ past participle. The object becomes the subject: “The new proposal has been rejected by the committee.”
